unit: Unit 1: AS 12 Accounting for Government Grants
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction & Definition of Government Grants
explain: AS 12 prescribes accounting rules for government grants like subsidies, cash incentives, and duty drawbacks.
Government grants are assistance in cash or kind given for past or future compliance with specified conditions.
Grants exclude assistance that cannot be valued reasonably and normal trading transactions with government.
The standard does not cover changing prices, non-grant government assistance, or government equity participation.
Proper accounting is vital to show how much an enterprise benefited from government support during the period.

flow.title: Identifying a Government Grant under AS 12
steps: Ensure value can be measured reasonably
Confirm it is not normal trading

topics.example: A state government grants ₹10 lakhs to a textile company for installing eco-friendly machinery.
remember: Government participation in equity ownership is EXCLUDED from AS 12.
mistakes: Treating normal government procurement or commercial trading transactions as government grants.

quiz.q: Which of the following is specifically excluded from the scope of AS 12?
o: Cash subsidies for setting up factories
quiz.why: AS 12 explicitly excludes government participation in the ownership of an enterprise from its scope.

quiz.q: Government grants exclude forms of assistance that:
o: Cannot reasonably have a value placed upon them
quiz.why: Assistance where a reasonable value cannot be assigned is excluded from the definition of government grants.

topics.title: Accounting Approaches & Recognition Criteria
explain: Two main accounting approaches exist: Capital Approach and Income Approach.
Under Capital Approach, grants are treated as part of shareholders' funds (Capital Reserve).
Under Income Approach, grants are recognized in the Profit & Loss statement over one or more periods.
Grants are recognized ONLY when there is reasonable assurance of meeting conditions AND receiving the grant.
Mere physical receipt of a grant is not conclusive proof that attached conditions will be fulfilled.

flow.title: Grant Recognition Decision Flow
steps: Is there assurance grant is received?
If BOTH YES, recognize in books

topics.example: X Ltd applies for a local grant with conditions it might fail to meet. X Ltd must NOT recognize the grant until compliance is reasonably assured.
remember: 2 core conditions for recognition: Reasonable assurance of compliance + Reasonable assurance of receipt.
mistakes: Recognizing a grant in the books merely because cash was received, even when condition compliance is doubtful.

quiz.q: A government grant is recognized in accounts only when there is reasonable assurance that:
o: Cash is deposited in the bank
The enterprise will comply with conditions and the grant will be received
The board of directors approves the grant
The tax department issues a clearance certificate
quiz.why: AS 12 requires reasonable assurance of both condition compliance and grant receipt before recognition.

quiz.q: Is the physical receipt of a grant conclusive evidence that attached conditions will be fulfilled?
o: No, receipt alone is not conclusive evidence
Yes, if received from Central Government
Yes, provided it is credited to bank
quiz.why: According to AS 12, receipt of a grant is not of itself conclusive evidence of compliance with conditions.

topics.title: Non-Monetary Government Grants
explain: Non-monetary grants are assets given by government like land or resources at concessional rates or free.
If an asset is given at a concessional rate, it is recorded at its actual acquisition cost.
If a non-monetary asset is given free of cost, it is recorded at a nominal value in books.
Any registration or incidental cost paid for nominal grants forms part of the initial recorded cost.

flow.title: Accounting for Non-Monetary Grants
steps: If concessional: Record at actual cost paid
If free of cost: Record at nominal value

topics.example: A government gives land worth ₹20 crore to a school at a concessional price of ₹50 lakhs. The school records land at ₹50 lakhs.
remember: Free non-monetary assets = Record at Nominal Value.
Concessional assets = Record at Acquisition Cost.
mistakes: Recording a concessional asset at its full market value instead of its actual acquisition cost.

quiz.q: How should a non-monetary asset received free of cost from the government be recorded?
o: At historical cost of the government
It should not be recorded at all
quiz.why: AS 12 specifies that non-monetary assets given free of cost are recorded at a nominal value.

quiz.q: Government grants land worth ₹10 crore to Y Ltd at a concessional registration cost of ₹20 lakhs. Y Ltd records land at:
quiz.why: Assets given at concessional rates are accounted for at their actual acquisition cost paid (₹20 lakhs).

topics.title: Presentation of Grants Related to Specific Fixed Assets
explain: Grants for specific fixed assets require buying, constructing, or acquiring specified long-term assets.
Method I (Cost Reduction): Grant is deducted from gross asset value; lower depreciation is charged to P&L.
If grant covers 100% (or virtually all) asset cost under Method I, asset is shown at nominal value.
Method II (Deferred Income): Grant is credited to Deferred Income and transferred to P&L over useful life.
For non-depreciable assets under Method II, grant goes to Capital Reserve (unless obligations exist).

flow.title: Presentation Methods for Fixed Asset Grants
steps: Receive grant for specific fixed asset
Method I: Deduct grant from gross asset cost
Method II: Credit to Deferred Income Account
Amortize grant to P&L over useful life

topics.example: Z Ltd buys an asset for ₹50 lakhs (salvage ₹5 lakhs, life 5 yrs) and receives ₹10 lakhs grant. Method I reduces cost to ₹40 lakhs (depreciation ₹7 lakhs/yr). Method II keeps cost at ₹50 lakhs (depreciation ₹9 lakhs/yr) and amortizes ₹2 lakhs/yr deferred income.
remember: Method I reduces asset book value; Method II creates Deferred Income Account.
mistakes: Crediting a grant for a depreciable fixed asset directly to Capital Reserve under Method II instead of Deferred Income.

quiz.q: Under Method I, how is a government grant related to a specific fixed asset presented in financial statements?
o: Deducted from the gross value of the asset
Shown as a liability on the Balance Sheet
Recognized as Other Income in year 1
quiz.why: Method I shows the grant as a deduction from the gross value of the concerned asset.

quiz.q: Under Method II, a government grant for a depreciable fixed asset is recognized in P&L:
o: Immediately in the year of receipt
On a systematic basis over the useful life of the asset
When the asset is fully disposed of
Equal to the total purchase price of the asset
quiz.why: Method II treats the grant as deferred income and allocates it to P&L over the asset's useful life.

topics.title: Presentation of Grants Related to Revenue
explain: Revenue grants are given to meet recurring operational expenses or compensate for losses.
Presentation Option A: Credit the grant in P&L separately or under 'Other Income'.
Presentation Option B: Deduct the grant directly from the related expense in P&L.
Grants spanning multiple years are held in Deferred Income and credited to P&L on a systematic basis.

flow.title: Accounting Choice for Revenue Grants
steps: Option A: Credit under Other Income in P&L
Option B: Deduct from related expense in P&L

topics.example: A hospital receives ₹90 lakhs lump-sum grant for 5 years of salary expense (₹30 lakhs/yr). Each year, ₹18 lakhs is recognized in P&L as income or offset against salary expense.
remember: Revenue grants can be shown as 'Other Income' OR deducted from the related expense.
mistakes: Recognizing a multi-year lump-sum revenue grant fully as income in Year 1 instead of spreading it over relevant periods.

quiz.q: Which of the following is an acceptable presentation for a grant related to revenue?
o: Deducted from the related expense in Profit & Loss
quiz.why: AS 12 allows revenue grants to be credited as Other Income or deducted from the related expense.

quiz.q: Co X receives a ₹90 lakh revenue grant covering salary expenses for 5 years. Annual recognition in P&L on SLM is:
quiz.why: ₹90 lakhs divided equally over 5 years equals ₹18 lakhs per annum.

topics.title: Grants in the Nature of Promoters' Contribution
explain: Promoters' contribution grants are given towards total capital outlay or total outlay in backward areas.
No repayment is ordinarily expected for such subsidies (e.g., Central Investment Subsidy Scheme).
These grants are treated as Capital Reserve and form part of shareholders' funds.
Capital Reserve created from such grants CANNOT be distributed as dividend nor taken as deferred income.

flow.title: Promoters' Contribution Accounting Flow
steps: Receive grant for total capital investment
Credit full amount to Capital Reserve

topics.example: Top & Top Ltd receives ₹10 crore subsidy (20% of ₹50 crore investment in backward area). It must credit ₹10 crore to Capital Reserve, not P&L.
remember: Promoters' contribution = Capital Reserve (Not P&L, Not Dividend).
mistakes: Treating a promoter's contribution subsidy as revenue income to reduce current accounting losses.

quiz.q: Grants in the nature of promoters' contribution must be credited to:
o: Profit & Loss Account as Other Income
quiz.why: AS 12 requires grants in the nature of promoters' contribution to be credited to Capital Reserve.

quiz.q: Can a Capital Reserve created from a government grant in the nature of promoters' contribution be distributed as dividend?
o: No, it can neither be distributed as dividend nor considered deferred income
Yes, up to 50% of the grant amount
quiz.why: AS 12 explicitly states such capital reserves cannot be distributed as dividend or considered deferred income.

topics.title: Refund of Government Grants
explain: Grants become refundable if attached compliance conditions are violated.
A grant refund is treated as an extraordinary item as per AS 5.
Revenue Grant Refund: Applied first against unamortized deferred credit balance; any excess is charged to P&L.
Fixed Asset Grant Refund (Method I): Asset book value is increased; prospective depreciation charged over remaining life.
Fixed Asset Grant Refund (Method II): Reduces deferred income balance; excess charged to P&L.
Promoters' Contribution Refund: Amount recoverable by government is deducted from Capital Reserve.

flow.title: Refund Processing Steps
steps: Revenue: Reduce Deferred Credit first, balance to P&L
Fixed Asset: Increase asset book value or reduce deferred income

topics.example: Asset bought for ₹20 lakhs (grant ₹8 lakhs net cost ₹12 lakhs, life 4 yrs, residual ₹4 lakhs). Year 1 dep = ₹2 lakhs (BV ₹10 lakhs). Year 2 refund ₹5 lakhs increases BV to ₹15 lakhs. Revised dep = (15-4)/3 = ₹3.67 lakhs/yr.
remember: Refund is an EXTRAORDINARY ITEM (AS 5). Asset cost adjustment requires PROSPECTIVE depreciation.
mistakes: Recalculating depreciation retrospectively instead of prospectively when a fixed asset grant is refunded.

quiz.q: How is a refund of a government grant treated in the financial statements?
quiz.why: AS 12 mandates treating grant refunds as extraordinary items in accordance with AS 5.

quiz.q: When a revenue grant becomes refundable, the refund amount is applied first against:
o: Any unamortized deferred credit remaining for that grant
quiz.why: The refund of a revenue grant is first set off against unamortized deferred credit, with any excess debited to P&L.

topics.title: Disclosure Requirements
explain: Entities must disclose the specific accounting policy adopted for government grants.
The presentation methods used in financial statements must be explicitly stated.
Entities must disclose the nature and extent of government grants recognized.
Grants of non-monetary assets given at concessional rates or free of cost must also be disclosed.

flow.title: AS 12 Disclosure Checklist
steps: Disclose nature & extent of grants recognized

topics.example: A company notes in its financial statements: 'Government grants related to fixed assets are deducted from gross book value under AS 12; non-monetary land received at ₹50 lakhs concessional rate is disclosed.'
remember: Must disclose both Accounting Policy AND Nature & Extent of grants received.
mistakes: Omitting disclosure of free or concessional non-monetary assets thinking they have zero or negligible impact.

quiz.q: Which of the following disclosures is required under AS 12?
o: Names of government officers approving the grant
Accounting policy adopted, including presentation methods used
Tax exemption status of government officials
Market value of all self-constructed assets
quiz.why: AS 12 requires clear disclosure of accounting policies and presentation methods used for grants.

quiz.q: Does AS 12 require disclosure of non-monetary assets given free of cost or at concessional rates?
o: No, non-monetary grants are exempt from disclosure
Yes, nature and extent of such grants must be disclosed
Only if market value exceeds ₹50 crore
quiz.why: AS 12 explicitly requires disclosing the nature and extent of non-monetary grants given free or at concessional rates.
